document_metadata.document_title: Wayne County Stormwater Control Program — Standards Manual

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: First Flush / WQC: remove ≥80% TSS or limit peak TSS to 80 mg/L for the first 1.0 inch of rainfall. CPVC: infiltrate first 1.0 inch of rainfall where soils/groundwater permit. CPRC: store and release volume from a 1.9-inch storm over ≥48 hours.
peak_flow_calculation_method: 100-year flood control: ≤0.15 cfs/acre for drainage areas ≥100 acres
Variable release rate curve for areas <100 acres (0.15–1.0 cfs/acre)
Detention / retention systems with flow restrictors

evidence.page_or_section: 6.3.1 First Flush Treatment / CPVC waiver, page 43-45

evidence.excerpt: Each bioretention cell is designed with the maximum 12-inch ponding depth
The permanent pool in a traditional detention basin must be a minimum of 4 feet deep.
Store and release the volume generated by a 1.9-inch storm event for a discharge duration of 48 hours
Extended Detention means the storage and gradual release of stormwater from a detention system over a period of not less than 48 hours.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Pipeline excerpt repair removed 1 unlocated citation(s).

design_parameters.enrich_notes: CPVC tied to 1-inch rainfall volume (VCPVC = A * C * 3630 ft³); active infiltration credited over six hours for bioretention. CPRC uses 1.9-inch storm released over ≥48 hours. In-situ infiltration thresholds: BMPs not permitted below 0.10 in/hr; CPVC waiver when below 0.24 in/hr or GW within 2 ft of BMP bottom. Forebay first-flush release over 24 hours. Traditional detention permanent pool minimum 4 ft; constructed wetland pool 0.5–3.0 ft by vegetation. Retention basin max storage depth 6 ft. Permeable pavement design deferred to DWSD manual.
